Add Criterion("n_trades", ">=", 100) as a default for strategy proposals; below that, PF confidence intervals are too wide to act on (at p = 0.5, 100 trades gives a standard error of 0.05 on the win rate alone).

Declare the whole search. When a child or Mandel searches strategy variants, the search harness, not the author, counts trials: every parameter set, indicator swap and filter evaluated increments n_trials, which is written to Proposal.n_trials_declared and consumed by deflated_sharpe_ratio. A proposal whose declared trial count is lower than the harness's log fails integrity (check_integrity). This converts "1,368 tests, 277 passed" from a boast into a deflation factor.

Incubation as a pre-registered gate stage. Add a lifecycle state between decided and live: incubating, with a pre-registered window defined in trades, not days (min_incubation_trades, default 100, or fewer only if the decision rule is pre-registered), recorded against the hypothetical fills of the dry-run executor using the same cost model as the backtest. Pass criteria pre-registered at preregister(): live pf_net above a floor derived from the backtest's bootstrap 10th percentile; live drawdown inside the backtest's 95th-percentile drawdown; live trade frequency within ±50% of the backtest's (a frequency mismatch means the signal is firing on different conditions than it was tested on, i.e. a repaint or data mismatch). Incubating candidates are never re-ranked and re-selected against each other on their incubation results alone; the incubation decision is per-candidate against its own pre-registered thresholds, otherwise incubation becomes one more selection step.

Expected-range monitoring with a kill switch (the risk agent, done as code). For each live strategy, derive from its accepted backtest: the trade-level win rate p and P&L distribution; bootstrap B equity paths of length n (block bootstrap over trades, block_bootstrap_pvalue already exists) to get the 5th-percentile equity, the 95th-percentile drawdown and the 99th-percentile losing streak (P(streak ≥ k in n trades) ≈ n·(1−p)^k). A monitor loop compares the live window with these bands and writes a ledger event on each breach. Pre-registered actions: one band breached → demote (size ÷ 2, alert the user); two bands or the equity floor → disable (executor refuses new orders for that strategy; open positions managed by the executor's own stops). Re-enabling is a new proposal through the gate. The LLM may be asked to *investigate* a breach and draft the post-mortem, but the breach detection and the disable are deterministic.

Decision-time data discipline. Every feature a signal reads carries an available_at timestamp; the backtest harness refuses features with available_at > decision_ts. For the arb bot this covers book snapshots, cross-venue quotes and any resolution or settlement information. This is the generalisation of "no multi-timeframe" and of resource 13's filtered-vs-smoothed rule.

Risk limits in the executor only. max_position_per_market, max_order_size, per-strategy capital caps and daily-loss limits are enforced in the order-placement path with their own tests; the signal layer may propose, the executor disposes. Stop logic for any directional position is placed as a resting order at the venue when the venue supports it; otherwise the executor polls at a bounded interval and the bound is part of the risk model.

Per-strategy capital isolation. Each accepted strategy gets a capital_cap and the executor tracks exposure per strategy; a new child's strategy starts at a cap proportional to its incubation evidence (e.g. 1% of capital per 100 incubation trades at pass, bounded).

Diversification as a measured object. Keep a rolling correlation matrix of per-strategy daily P&L; report the effective number of independent strategies N_eff = (Σλ_i)² / Σλ_i² from its eigenvalues (resource 10's PCA). A proposal to add a strategy whose P&L correlates above 0.7 with an incumbent is scored as a parameter change to the incumbent, not as a new edge.

Promotional-source handling. Add a provenance.incentive field to knowledge records (independent, vendor, vendor-with-product-in-loop). Claims from the last class enter as hypotheses with zero prior weight; only mechanisms (rules, formulas, failure modes) are adopted, never numbers.

Failure-mode checklist the gate must be able to test, drawn from this genre. Overfitting of parameters (optimizer sweeps: require walk-forward or combinatorial purged CV; report PBO = share of CSCV splits where the in-sample winner lands in the bottom half out-of-sample); selection across many candidates (DSR with the harness's trial count; Harvey–Liu-style haircut on t-stats); look-ahead/repainting (decision-time timestamps, item 6); survivorship and instrument selection (universe must be fixed before the search: altcoins that trended are not a universe); regime dependence (holdout windows must include at least one adverse regime; report performance by regime); fees and slippage (item 1); small live samples (minimum trade counts, item 2); leverage and compounding in reported returns (report un-levered, un-compounded per-trade statistics alongside the equity curve); metric gaming (PF with few trades; win rate with wide stops: require the quartet); execution mismatch (alert latency, partial fills: simulate from the book, not the mid); LLM test-window leakage (item 4: incubation on data that did not exist at selection time is the only clean test).

Ledger as scoreboard. The ledger already records every proposal, decision and rollback. Add the live P&L stream per strategy, including losses, open exposure and the monitor's band breaches, and make the public-facing summary (mandel/viz) draw from the ledger, not from a curated list, so Mandel's "scoreboard" is the thing the creator promises and cannot be shown to deliver.

Roughness is an exponent, not an adjective. "Fractals are rough. We can make that quantitative!" Any time Mandel or a child says a series, an error surface or a market is "noisy", "choppy" or "fractal", the statement must be replaced by a measured scaling exponent with an error bar and a scale range, because an exponent can be compared, tested against a null and tracked over time, and an adjective cannot.

Define by a scaling law, then measure by a procedure. The video's method is: generalise a concept through a property that survives generalisation (measure ∝ s^D), then supply a measurement procedure (box counting) that returns the number without assuming the structure. Mandel applies this template to its own constructs (edge, calibration, skill): each must have a definition that does not presuppose the model and a procedure that measures it on raw data, because a quantity that can only be read off from within the model that predicts it cannot falsify that model.

Exact recurrence is the exception; statistical recurrence is the claim. Self-similar fractals are a subset of fractals. Mandel does not look for the same pattern to recur at every scale in markets or in its own performance; it looks for the same *statistics* of roughness to recur, and tests that with scaling exponents rather than pattern matching, because exact recurrence is a knife-edge property that noise destroys while scaling statistics are robust.

Fit power laws in log space and report the slope with its range. Raw counts that "look parabolic" are unreadable; log N against log s is a straight line whose slope is the quantity of interest. Every exponent Mandel reports (edge versus horizon, error versus sample size, volatility versus time scale) is estimated as a regression slope in log-log coordinates, from many points, with a bootstrap confidence interval and the ε range stated, because the video's own "ManyBritainCounts" scene shows that one ratio is not an estimate.

Dimension is a function of scale; always state the scale. "Different slopes at different scales" and "2D at a distance, 1D up close". A property measured at one resolution does not transfer to another, so every measurement Mandel stores carries the resolution range it was made at, and a claimed invariant is tested for slope changes (crossovers) across that range before it is called invariant.

A fine grid is the same as a large scaling. Refining resolution and enlarging the object are one operation. For Mandel this means that "more data at the same resolution" and "the same data at a finer resolution" are different experiments with different questions, and the substrate must record which one was run, because conflating them is the usual way an in-sample exponent is mistaken for an out-of-sample one.

Two idealisations, and nature in the middle. Smooth (Gaussian, continuous, differentiable) and perfectly self-similar (power-law, scale-free) are both models. Mandel tags each model it uses with which idealisation it rests on and the scale range over which that idealisation was checked, because the error of a Gaussian model and the error of a power-law model are both measurable and the choice between them is an empirical one per scale range.

"Made up but useful" is the standard for a construct. Fractal dimension is admitted because it measures something and makes distinctions (Britain versus Norway) that matter. Mandel's own invented quantities (insight confidence, child trust, idea-market prices) earn their place only by the same test: they must predict something measurable out of sample, because a construct that distinguishes nothing is nomenclature.

Several estimators, record which one. Box-counting, information, Hausdorff and packing dimensions agree on nice sets and disagree on pathological ones. Mandel records the estimator and its settings (grid, offsets, ε range) as part of the provenance of any exponent, and treats disagreement between estimators as a flag that the object is not "nice", because an exponent without its estimator is not reproducible.

Ask "what slope does this approach?", not "what is the slope here?" The thought experiment of Britain becoming smooth at fine scales (slope bending to 1) is the right test: a fractal claim is a claim about the *trend* of the slope as resolution increases, within the measured range. Mandel's validation of any scale-free claim includes the finest and coarsest scales available and checks whether the slope is drifting towards the trivial value, because the interesting failure mode is not "the exponent is wrong" but "the exponent is converging to boring".

Reject "a fractal is a shape with non-integer dimension" as a definition, as the video itself does ("Kind of..."). Integer-dimensional fractals exist: the boundary of the Mandelbrot set has Hausdorff dimension 2 (Shishikura), the trail of planar Brownian motion has dimension 2, the Peano and Hilbert curves have dimension 2. Mandelbrot's definition is Hausdorff dimension strictly greater than topological dimension; the video's operational version (slope stays above the topological dimension across scales) is the one to use.

Hold loosely the specific coastline numbers. Britain 1.21 in the video versus 1.25 in Richardson–Mandelbrot for the west coast; Norway 1.52 on screen versus 1.5 in the code; both outlines were synthesised to those values. Treat them as illustrative magnitudes. Any coastline-style number Mandel uses must come with dataset, method and range.

Hold loosely the gallery values 1.668 and 1.843. They were read off first iterations and are wrong in the limit (about 1.672 and 1.675). The lesson Mandel keeps is methodological: an exponent estimated from one stage of a process is not the exponent of the process.

Reject the inference "markets are fractal, therefore scale-free models apply at every scale". The video's own content forbids it: dimension depends on the scale window, and empirical power laws hold only over finite ranges. [general] Avnir, Biham, Lidar and Malcai (Science 279:39–40, 1998, "Is the geometry of nature fractal?") surveyed empirical fractal reports and found scaling ranges of only about one to two decades on average (the specific figure, roughly 1.3 decades, is from memory and not verified against the paper here); Mandelbrot's reply (Science 279:783) disputed the standard but not the finiteness. A market exponent is a statement about a declared range of time scales, nothing more.

Hold loosely "Non-integer dimension ⇔ Roughness" as an equivalence. It is a good one-line reading for curves in the plane, where dimension 1 means smooth and values towards 2 mean area-filling, but roughness in time series is better carried by the Hurst exponent or the variogram exponent, and for multifractal objects a single number is not enough (a spectrum is). Resource #13's volatility-clustering remark lives here.

Hold loosely the flow chart "fractal → probably from nature, not fractal → probably man-made". It is a heuristic about growth processes versus design, not a theorem; markets are both (human rules at round numbers, deadlines, and settlement times impose man-made smooth structure on rough order flow), so Mandel should expect mixed scaling with crossovers rather than a clean verdict.

Reject box-counting on small samples without a null. The strict box dimension of any finite set is 0; what is estimated is a slope over a range, biased by finite size and sensitive to grid placement. [general] The graph of a memoryless random walk has box dimension 1.5 (D = 2 − H with H = 1/2); any claim that a price path's roughness carries information must beat that null out of sample, consistent with #09's rule.

Hold loosely the box-counting dimension as a stand-in for Hausdorff dimension. They coincide for the video's examples and differ for sets like the rationals (0 versus 1); since Mandel only ever works with finite data the distinction is academic, but the estimator must be named.

Hold loosely the video's implicit claim that the Britain log-log plot shows a constant slope "always > 1". The scene is a demonstration on synthetic data; for the real coastline there is a lower cutoff (tidal definition, grain size) below which the question is ill-posed, and an upper cutoff at the size of the island. Every empirical fractal has both cutoffs.

A ScalingEstimate record (new, in mandel/validation/). Resource #09's file already refers to such a record; it does not exist yet (no hit for ScalingEstimate, box_count or hurst in the code). Minimal schema, in the spirit of the video's log-log plot: quantity (what was counted or measured), scales (the list of ε or s values), values (N(ε) or the measured quantity), log_slope, log_intercept, slope_ci (block-bootstrap over windows), r2, n_decades = log10(max ε / min ε), estimator (box-count, variogram, DFA, rescaled range), estimator_settings (grid offsets averaged, detrending order), null_value (e.g. 1.5 for a random-walk graph, 0.5 for the Hurst exponent), null_rejected (CI excludes the null), crossover_detected (see item 3), holdout_id, as_of. The gate's Criterion(metric, comparator, threshold) can then reference n_decades, slope_ci_width, null_rejected directly.

Validation rule: no exponent without a range. An exponent is reportable to children or stored as an insight only if n_decades >= 1.0 (declared per quantity; 1.5 preferred), slope_ci excludes null_value, and the ε range is stated. This is the Avnir caveat made into a gate criterion, and it is what the video's "Better fit at higher inputs" caption is pointing at: coarse-grid counts are noisy and the asymptotic regime must actually be reached.

Crossover test ("different slopes at different scales"). Fit a single line and a two-segment piecewise line to the log-log data; if the two-segment fit wins by a declared BIC margin, set crossover_detected = True, store both slopes with their ranges, and refuse to summarise the object by one exponent. The coil (1D, 3D, 1D) is the canonical case; for markets, the expected analogue is a change of roughness exponent between intraday and multi-day horizons.

The scale-consistent edge criterion (ORIGINAL-IDEAS §3) gets its mechanism. Compute edge (Brier skill versus market, or excess return) at several coarse-grainings of the same held-out data (per question, per category, per week, per month, per platform) and add Criterion("n_scales_agree", ">=", k) to forecast_improvement_criteria and strategy_improvement_criteria. The video's justification is item 15 above: a real property shows the same slope as resolution changes; a searched-for artefact lives at one scale. Falsification condition as already written in ORIGINAL-IDEAS: multi-scale survivors fail out of sample no less often than single-scale survivors.

Resolution versus sample size, logged separately. Because "a fine grid is the same as a large scaling", every backtest and forecast evaluation records both the data resolution (bar size, forecast horizon) and the sample length, and a proposal that changes one must say so. The gate already demands out_of_sample and n_trials; add resolution and n_decades_of_horizon to the evidence dictionary built by evidence_from_comparison.

Model cards carry their idealisation. Each model or scoring rule in the repo (Gaussian bootstrap, block bootstrap, HMM regimes, any power-law or Hurst feature) is tagged idealisation: smooth | scale-free | mixed and validated_scale_range. A model used outside its validated range triggers a warning in the gate rationale. This is the "Nature / idealised as smooth / idealised as self-similar" picture turned into metadata.

Box counting as a coverage diagnostic for Mandel itself (Mandel's inference, hold loosely). Treat the space of prediction-market questions as a grid (category × horizon × platform × liquidity bucket) and count "boxes touched" by Mandel's resolved forecasts at several granularities. If N(ε) grows with an exponent well below the dimension of the grid, Mandel's coverage is clustered (fractal) rather than space-filling, which is a measurable statement of where its blind spots are. Report coverage_exponent on the dashboard; do not gate on it until it has predicted something (adopt item 8).

Roughness features for children are gated, not assumed. A child (Hurst is already a reserved name in children.py) may estimate roughness exponents of price paths; Mandel accepts such a feature only through a pre-registered proposal whose evidence includes a ScalingEstimate with null_rejected = True on held-out data and a positive skill_vs_market. The concept-graph regex for fractal_dimension in graph.py already clusters these terms; the gate is what keeps the cluster honest.

Every stored exponent is a slope with provenance, never a number. In the knowledge files and the ledger, write exponents as D = 1.21 ± 0.04 over 3 km–300 km, box-count, 8 grid offsets, source X and never as D = 1.21. The video's own two gallery mistakes came from skipping exactly this discipline.

"What slope does this approach?" as a convergence check for Mandel's own loop. Plot Mandel's held-out error against cumulative evidence (cycles, resolved questions) in log-log coordinates. A learning loop that is working shows a steady negative slope; one that is fitting noise shows a slope bending towards 0 as the sample grows (the "eventually smooth" picture). Add error_scaling_slope to the cycle summary in cycles.py and review it at each renormalisation level (ORIGINAL-IDEAS §7).

Estimator disagreement is a recorded event. When two roughness estimators (say box-count and variogram) on the same data give CIs that do not overlap, write a ledger event rather than averaging them. Resource #09 adopts the same rule for Brier versus log loss; this file supplies the geometric case where the disagreement is a theorem (Hausdorff versus box dimension can differ).

Synthetic demonstrations are labelled as such. The video's Britain curve was generated to have slope 1.21. Mandel's test fixtures (synthetic price paths with a chosen Hurst exponent, synthetic forecast sets with chosen calibration) are legitimate for testing estimators, but every result produced on them is tagged data_kind: synthetic and cannot enter the insight store as evidence about markets.

Keep parameter space and dynamical space as two different planes, with an explicit dictionary between them. Because every confusion in the subject comes from mixing the c-plane with the z-plane: M is a picture of parameter space whose every point is a whole dynamical system, and Mandel's catalogue of strategy and model settings is likewise a space whose every point is a whole behaviour, to be kept apart from the market state those behaviours act on.

Find the critical orbit: one diagnostic trajectory decides the global class. Because K_c is connected or dust according to the orbit of the single critical point; Mandel should identify, for each strategy class, the one cheapest quantity whose out-of-sample trajectory decides membership in the validated set, and run it before any full backtest.

Study the exterior to understand the interior. Because Φ_M, the rays and the whole combinatorics come from the dynamics for c outside M ("the basic idea is to find properties of M by a careful study of the dynamics for parameter values outside of M"); the structure of what works is mapped by the structure of what fails, so rejected proposals are data to be organised, not waste.

Name every point by its angle: addresses computed from the dynamics, not assigned by hand. Because external arguments are computed from the itinerary (binary digits) and two parameters with the same argument pattern are the same parameter (Metropolis–Stein–Stein); Mandel's identifiers for decisions and insights should be derived from their evidence itinerary so that identical reasoning is recognised as identical and near-identical reasoning is adjacent.

Record validated regions, each with a centre, a root and a multiplier, rather than single best settings. Because a hyperbolic component is a region of parameter space with one stable qualitative behaviour, uniformised by the multiplier (how strongly attracting), with a centre (the best-behaved point) and a root (where it bifurcated from its parent); the same three coordinates describe a validated region of Mandel's settings: the margin by which the gate held, the settings with the largest margin, and the proposal it grew out of.

Treat boundaries as where behaviour changes: the bifurcation locus is ∂M. Because every delicate object (parabolic points, Misiurewicz points, dimension 2) lives on the boundary and a small move across it changes the qualitative outcome; a candidate near a known region boundary needs more out-of-sample evidence than one deep inside.

Renormalise honestly: a sub-loop may reuse the parent's theory only after a straightening check, and should expect a homeomorphic copy with different decorations. Because Douady–Hubbard reuse the quadratic theory inside a small copy only when the restricted iterate is polynomial-like (U' relatively compact in U, proper, degree 2), and the copies are homeomorphic, not similar; ORIGINAL-IDEAS #7 ("the same loop at four scales") needs analogous conditions before a child's inner loop inherits Mandel's gate, and must re-derive its budgets and thresholds rather than copy them.

Expect universality, then test it. Because copies of M appear in every analytic family (McMullen), so the same region/centre/root/boundary structure should appear in every child's parameter space, but the theorem gives quasiconformal copies, not identical settings; transfer between children or markets requires a transfer test (A1's lesson).

Hold conjectures as first-class objects with status, implications and partial results. Because the Orsay notes open by stating MLC and HG2, prove MLC ⇒ HG2, and footnote what Yoccoz later proved; Mandel's store should hold its open hypotheses the same way: statement, what they would imply, what is proved so far, and what would decide them.

Pictures suggest theorems; the gate decides. Because pictures misled Mandelbrot on connectedness and later suggested the small copies, MLC and dimension 2, and in every case the proof came afterwards; the signal map and backtest plots are generators of hypotheses, never evidence.

Prefer the weakest structure that lets the proofs be copied. Because polynomial-like maps were invented on noticing that "one uses the theory of analytic functions continually, but the rigidity of polynomials only rarely"; Mandel's abstractions (the child interface, the evaluator protocol, the proposal schema) should demand only what the validation argument actually uses, so that the same gate applies to new children without rewriting.

Markets are not holomorphic dynamics. z² + c predicts nothing about prices; the transferable content is the method (parameter space, stability regions, addresses from itineraries, renormalisation discipline), not the map, the set, or its pictures.

Visual resemblance between M or Julia sets and price charts is not evidence of anything. Tan Lei similarity and McMullen universality are theorems about holomorphic families with a conformal structure; time series have none.

Exact self-similarity of Mandel's own loop across scales (ORIGINAL-IDEAS #7) is an expectation to test, not a design fact. Copies of M are homeomorphic, not similar, and the infinitely renormalizable parameters are precisely the hard cases; if the levels need different procedures in practice the design should drop the analogy, as that idea's own falsification clause says.

"Every stable region has a mechanism" is the HG2 analogue and is unproved even for M. Mandel may find regions of settings that pass the gate with no identifiable reason (ghost components); it must label them as such and cap their confidence rather than invent a mechanism after the fact.

Clean escape criteria do not transfer. |z| > 2 implies escape because of algebra; there is no theorem that a strategy whose drawdown crosses a threshold never recovers, so Mandel's stop rules are budget decisions that must be pre-registered as decisions, not presented as laws.

The specifics of the 2013 colloquium are inferred. Venue (KAIST), order of topics and pictures come from a title string, a search snippet, and Hubbard's abstract for later talks of the same title; "What it says" is his programme, not a transcript.
Universality is not a licence to copy settings between children or markets. Existence of a copy of the structure is not identity of the parameters.
Do not cite MLC as settled. As of the sources read (January 2024 and earlier) it is open; Mandel re-checks before stating a status.

ParameterRegion record in the ProposalBook. Fields: target, strategy_id, param_ranges (the box of settings over which the gate held across the walk-forward windows), centre (the settings with the largest gate margin), root (the proposal id this region bifurcated from, with kind primitive or satellite), multiplier (the gate margin normalised to [0, 1), for example 1 − achieved/required deflated Sharpe, or the Brier-skill margin over the market), boundary (rejected neighbouring settings). A query region_map(target) returns regions, gaps and boundaries; a region is the unit of what Mandel claims to know about a strategy's settings.

Boundary flag in the gate. If a candidate's settings lie within one grid step of a rejected neighbour or of an accepted region's edge, the gate requires one additional out-of-sample window before deciding. Metrics: boundary_flag_rate (fraction of proposals flagged) and boundary_flip_rate (how often the extra window changed the verdict).

Critical-orbit probe before full evaluation. Each strategy class declares one critical quantity (for example rolling out-of-sample Brier skill against the market price at forecast time) and a pre-registered escape radius (a loss bound). The first, cheapest fold runs only the critical orbit; candidates that escape stop early and are logged with their escape time (folds survived), a continuous colouring like the escape-time algorithm, rather than a bare reject. This is the staged evaluation of A1 and A2 with a named diagnostic.

Itinerary identifiers next to provenance hashes. Every gate decision path is recorded as a binary string, one bit per stage or fold (pass or fail), stored with the proposal. Two proposals with identical itineraries and the same provenance class are flagged as candidate duplicates; the prefix order on itineraries retrieves the nearest prior decision when a new proposal arrives, so negative results are found by address rather than by search.

Straightening check for ORIGINAL-IDEAS #7. Before a sub-scale loop (a child, a strategy inside a child, a single forecast) reuses the parent gate, three conditions are checked and logged: domain (its data and budget are a proper subset of the parent's, the analogue of U' relatively compact in U), properness (each sub-proposal maps to exactly one parent observation), degree (exactly one critical quantity). If any fails, the level receives its own written gate with its own thresholds. Metrics: renormalisation_depth (nested loops that passed) and straightening_failures.

Tuning operator for proposals. tune(P, Q) applies proposal Q inside the region validated by P; the result's region is recorded as P ∗ Q with lineage. The test suite checks associativity on recorded compositions ((P ∗ Q) ∗ R and P ∗ (Q ∗ R) must yield the same region), as a regression test that composing accepted changes is well defined.

Conjecture registry. A file mandel/state/conjectures.jsonl with entries {id, statement, status in {open, partial, proved, refuted}, implies [ids], partial_results [refs], deciding_metric, last_checked}, seeded with ORIGINAL-IDEAS #1-7 as conjectures (for #2: "Mandel's Brier score on its own proposals falls over the first fifty", with the metric and threshold named).

Exterior-first weekly job. Over rejected proposals compute a potential G = log(required_margin / achieved_margin), the distance outside the gate, and an angle, the itinerary prefix at which the proposal failed; report equipotential bands (how far from acceptance the rejects sit) and the distribution of angles (which failure modes dominate). Metric: median potential of rejects per target and its trend.

Ghost-region detector. Any accepted region whose proposal records no mechanism field (the stated reason the edge should exist) is counted as a ghost; the metric ghost_regions should be 0, and a ghost region's insights are capped at the inference-only confidence (0.5) until a mechanism is recorded and independently supported.

Signal-map parameter-space view. For a chosen strategy, plot the settings tried so far coloured by gate outcome and escape time, with accepted regions outlined and centres and roots marked; it is an instrument for choosing the next proposal (ORIGINAL-IDEAS #6), never evidence.

Metrics summary. regions_per_target, mean_multiplier of accepted regions, boundary_flag_rate, boundary_flip_rate, escape_time distribution, renormalisation_depth, straightening_failures, ghost_regions, median reject potential.
Archive with lineage, never a single champion. Every proposal, accepted or rejected, stays in the proposal book with its parent (supersedes), because the DGM's best agents descended through dips.

Sample what to try next from the whole archive, weighted by score and novelty. Mandel's idea-selection should use a DGM-style weight: sigmoid of expected gain times 1/(1 + times this line has already been tried), with a floor so no class is ever abandoned.
Staged evaluation. Cheap checks first (unit tests, a short backtest slice), full held-out evaluation only for candidates that clear them. This is how 80 iterations stay affordable.

The evaluator and its logs are produced by code the proposer cannot edit. Mandel's gate, ledger and evidence writers live outside anything a proposal may change; a proposal that touches them is refused by construction, because the DGM showed the model will edit the detector when it is in reach.
Treat benchmark gain as necessary, not sufficient. A passed gate earns adoption in dry-run, not live money (MANDEL.md principle 13).

Version the meta-level. The DGM could not improve its own exploration procedure. Mandel's proposer (prompts, checklists, selection weights) is versioned and gated like any other component, so its hit rate can be measured per version.

The USD 22,000 per run scale: Mandel's loop must be designed to make progress at two to three orders of magnitude less, which is why the staged evaluation and the bits-per-token budget matter more here than in the paper.
"Open-ended" as a goal in itself: Mandel's objective is validated predictive gain, so novelty is a selection bonus, not the objective.
Coding benchmarks as the fitness function: Mandel's fitness is out-of-sample forecast skill and net PnL, which resolve slowly and noisily; the archive will fill much more slowly than the DGM's.
ProposalBook: already keeps rejected proposals and the supersedes link; add a lineage() query that returns the tree for a hypothesis family and the dips along it.
Proposer selection weights: w = sigmoid(10·(expected_gain − 0.5)) / (1 + prior_attempts); log the weights so the honest n_trials_declared can be reconciled with realised attempts.
Evaluation cascade in the gate: code_change_criteria (tests) → short-window backtest → full walk-forward with embargo; a proposal records which stage it reached.
A "protected paths" list (gate, ledger, forecast book, evidence builders): a proposal whose change touches them is refused at draft.
Metrics: archive size, fraction of accepted proposals whose parent was rejected (stepping-stone rate), proposer hit rate per version.

Evaluator first. Nothing enters Mandel's improvement loop until it has an automatic scorer: for strategies the walk-forward comparison, for forecasters the forecast book's Brier and skill, for code the test suite. Components without a scorer are documented as not yet improvable.

Evolve-blocks. Each improvable component (edge estimator, sizing rule, fee model, calibration layer, the children's prompts) gets an explicit boundary; proposals may change only what is inside it. The skeleton, the gate and the evidence writers stay outside.
Cascade. Unit tests → short backtest slice → full held-out evaluation; most failures die cheaply. This is the operational form of principle 6 (information has a cost).
Several metrics at once. Record Brier, log loss, calibration error and net PnL together; a proposal that improves one by wrecking another is visible.
Diversity in the archive. Keep the best variant per niche (per market category, per horizon) rather than one global best, which is MAP-Elites applied to strategies.
The scale of search: AlphaEvolve samples thousands of programs; Mandel's budget allows tens of proposals per cycle, so the cascade must reject most candidates at the first stage.
LLM-graded evaluators for anything that feeds the gate: the paper itself did not optimise for them, and the DGM (A1) showed what happens when the judged party can touch the judge.
Months-long self-improvement loops: Mandel's cycle must close in days, with the forecast book providing resolutions continuously.
A scorers.py registry: each improvable component maps to a scorer and a cascade; draft refuses a proposal whose target has no scorer.
Evolve-block markers in the repo's strategy code (core/arb_engine.py edge calculation, sizing, fee model) so a child's proposals are scoped automatically.
Niche keys for the archive: (platform, category, horizon); ProposalBook.query by niche; the signal map can colour accepted proposals by niche.
Metrics: stage-1 rejection rate (should be high and cheap), cost per accepted proposal by stage, number of niches with an accepted variant.

Never rewrite the knowledge file wholesale. The insight store is already append-and-update with tombstones; the synthesis document is the one place a full rewrite is allowed, and it is regenerated from the store, not the other way round.

Helpful/harmful counters on every insight. Each time a proposal that depended on an insight passes or fails the gate, the insight's counters move; confidence updates come from counters, not from re-reading.

Separate the roles. Generator (the children and Mandel's proposers), Reflector (the post-mortem on each decided proposal), Curator (deterministic merge into the store). The Curator is code, not a model.
De-duplicate by meaning, lazily. Near-duplicate insights are merged when the store grows past a threshold, keeping provenance from both.

Feedback quality gates adaptation. Where Mandel has only weak signals (no resolutions yet, no backtest), it records candidates but does not adapt behaviour, because ACE's finance results show adaptation on noisy signals makes things worse.
Embedding-based de-duplication as the only merge rule: for claims about markets, two bullets can be semantically close and factually opposite; merge requires provenance agreement too.
Treating the Reflector as a single model call: Mandel's reflection on a failed proposal is a pre-registered checklist (look-ahead? fees? regime?) before any free-form reasoning.
Accuracy on agent benchmarks as a proxy for forecasting value; the mechanism transfers, the numbers do not.
Insight gains helpful: int, harmful: int; ProposalBook.decide increments them for every insight in depends_on_insights; update_confidence can be driven by a Beta posterior over the counters.
A reflect(proposal) step after every decision that writes a structured post-mortem (which assumption failed, which check caught it) as kind="procedure" insights with provenance proposal:<id>.
InsightStore.dedupe(threshold) with a provenance-agreement rule; log merges to the ledger.
SYNTHESIS.md is generated from validated insights plus the knowledge files, with a header stating the store version it was built from.
Metrics: insight churn per cycle, fraction of insights with non-zero counters, collapse guard (store size must not drop by more than a set fraction in one cycle without a logged reason).

Multifractality as a test, not a belief. When Mandel claims structure in a price series, it runs the partition-function test over at least two decades of Δt, reports τ(q) with a bootstrap band, and compares against a shuffled-series null, because Lux showed the unshuffled plot alone proves little.

Prefer the estimable model. The MSM is the version of Mandelbrot's idea that can be fitted, scored and forecast; Mandel implements the k-component volatility filter (k of 5 to 8 is tractable in numpy) as a volatility and regime feature, and tests it the same way as any other proposal.

One mechanism for several stylized facts beats one patch per fact. Fat tails, clustering and long memory from a single cascade is the kind of parsimony Mandel should look for in its own models and in the children's.

Longer horizons are where structure shows. The MSM's edge over GARCH grows from one day to fifty; Mandel's own multi-scale consistency test (ORIGINAL-IDEAS #3) should expect edges to be clearest at the coarser scales, not the finest.
The history is the lesson. A beautiful model that cannot be estimated is a hypothesis without a gate. Every model Mandel adopts must come with its estimator and its out-of-sample score.

Exact self-similarity or a fixed Hurst exponent for prediction-market prices: these series are bounded in [0, 1], event-driven and resolve, so scaling can only hold over limited ranges and must be measured, not assumed.

Hurst or τ(q) estimates on short windows as trading signals: finite-sample bias and variance are large (survey section 2.4; Weron 2002 on confidence intervals), so they are diagnostics with intervals, never bare numbers.
The "fractal markets" rhetoric (Peters) as settled science: the testable content is the scaling function and the MSM's forecasting record, nothing more.

mandel/validation/scaling.py (planned): partition_function(x, qs, dts), tau_q(...) with bootstrap bands, shuffle_null(...), and a multifractality_report that states whether concavity survives the null. Used as a diagnostic in the gate, never as a pass criterion on its own.

mandel/models/msm.py (planned): binomial MSM with k components, closed-form filter and likelihood, fit, forecast_variance(h); registered with a scorer (log score of realised variance at horizons 1, 5, 10, 50) so it can be gated.
Forecast-book integration: MSM-implied uncertainty as a feature for sizing (ORIGINAL-IDEAS #4) and as the dispersion baseline for the children's disagreement signal (#5).
Metrics: τ(q) concavity statistic with interval; MSM out-of-sample variance R² by horizon versus a GARCH(1,1) baseline; fraction of markets where multifractality survives the shuffled null.

The crowd (market) is the benchmark, not accuracy. Every forecaster on Mandel's scoreboard is measured by Brier against resolution and by skill against the market price at forecast time; already built into the forecast book.
Point-in-time retrieval. Any evidence a forecast uses must carry a timestamp before the forecast; retrieval schedules must not depend on when the question resolved.

Selective forecasting as a first-class strategy. A forecaster may abstain; the scoreboard tracks coverage and skill on the questions it chose. Mandel should expect edge, if any, where the market is uncertain and information is fresh, and no edge where the market is confident.
Keep what beats the crowd, with a distance cap. Training signal comes from forecasts that beat the market by a bounded margin, not from extreme contrarian hits.
Ensemble by trimmed mean. The default pooling rule for the children's forecasts, re-tested against log-opinion pooling as ORIGINAL-IDEAS #5 proposes.
Fine-tuning as the route to improvement: Mandel runs on frozen weights; the equivalent is curating the retrieval and reasoning scaffold and the archive of reasonings that beat the market.

The headline "approaching human level": the system loses to the crowd overall (.179 vs .149) and only wins in a selected regime; Mandel should quote the selective numbers with the coverage they imply.
i.i.d. standard errors on resolved questions; Mandel's bootstrap must block by time, as the engine already does for returns.
Forecast records gain evidence_cutoff_ts and abstained: bool; the scoreboard reports coverage alongside skill.

A per-forecaster "regime table": skill versus market bucketed by market price (0.3–0.7 vs the tails), by question age and by evidence count, so guidance to a child can say where it should and should not forecast.

A reasoning archive: each forecast stores its rationale; rationales from forecasts that beat the market by less than a cap become retrieval material for later forecasts (the frozen-weights version of the paper's fine-tuning).
Gate criterion for a forecaster: Brier skill versus market > 0 on at least N resolved questions in the regime it claims, with a time-blocked bootstrap interval excluding zero.
Metrics: coverage, skill by regime, calibration RMS, fraction of questions where the pooled children beat the market.
